quest.title: O Archon, Have I Done Right?
quest.description: The shrine that Shouta has been giving sincere offerings to has stopped giving him replies. He seeks you out for help...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Ugh... This isn't good...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: We gave two offerings to the shrine, right? However, the deity hasn't responded to me yet.

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: I went to have a look, and offerings weren't there anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: But when we went there the first time, the deity granted a part of my wish after accepting my offerings...

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: So, I was thinking... Someone... Or something might've stolen the offerings before the deity could accept them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's a possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: If that's the case, then I'm in trouble. I might not be able to give offerings again...

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: If I'm too persistent with my wishes, even deities will grow impatient.

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Please help me! Please come with me to the shrine outside the city and take a look!

talks.objective: Go to the shrine outside the city

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: You thieves! The deity isn't replying to me because you stole all my offerings!

dialogues.speaker: Sarcastic Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: Offerings? Are you talking about the things that were placed beside the shrine? Please, we wouldn't want those things even if you gifted them to us!

dialogues.speaker: Sarcastic Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: Also, if you're offering that kind of rubbish to the shrine, it'd be funny if the deity replied to you at all!

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Wh—What did you say!? My offerings aren't rubbish!

dialogues.speaker: Sarcastic Treasure Hoarder
dialogues.text: Forget it, we don't have the time to play around with you!

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: M—My offerings aren't rubbish...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you tell us your wishes?

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Fine... Since things have turned out like this, I guess my wish won't be granted anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: My two wishes are simple. My first wish is that I don't want to take exams anymore! If I don't have to take exams, then I won't be scolded.

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: The other one is... I wish that the meanie at school will stop bullying me...

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: Right! Exams are dreadful... But that meanie makes me even more uncomfortable...

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: She saw me many times while I was making a wish at the shrine. When she overheard me saying I don't want to take exams, she went to my teachers and asked for my results.

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: From then on, she'd always tell me that my time is better spent paying attention in class rather than praying to a shrine. She also said if I'm that naggy, even deities will get impatient.

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: She even said that I'm being... really pathetic.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, it's not good to depend on the deity too much.

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: But when the adults face hardship, they always make offerings at the shrine...

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: Hmm... I don't get it... I thought everyone gave offerings to the shrines to ask for the god's help?

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: Let's go ask someone else.

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: Hmmm... Okay. Either way, my wishes won't be granted now...

choices.text: In the end, they still have to solve their problems themselves.

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: She's a person that's in my class. Sh—she's totally unreasonable!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are they... Treasure Hoarders? Why are they here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could they be the ones stealing the offerings?

talks.objective: Help Shouta find out the reason

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Hello, what can I help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the offerings at the shrine...

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Oh... The shrines... I've been there a few times as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: Hehe, I want the deity's blessings so that after I grow up, I can go to the outside world and see what it's like.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: However, at the end of the day, the offerings are only a form of prayer. I still need to work hard.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: My parents told me if I want to travel, I must earn enough money first...

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Yeah, as long as you have the deity's blessings, your dreams will come true!

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: I can't say that for sure. After all, if I really did go to the outside world, I don't think Inazuma's deities would be able to protect me.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: My parents used to say that giving offerings to the deities is just getting some peace of mind. If you want to fulfill your wishes, then it still depends on how much hard work you put in.

dialogues.speaker: Kouichi
dialogues.text: I can't really explain things that well. If you guys want to know more, then have a talk with Nanatsuki. She's quite knowledgeable in these things.

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Hmm... C'mon, let's go find Nanatsuki...

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: Shouta? Why do you look so upset? Did someone bully you?

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Nanatsuki, you must know how everyone in the city gives offerings to the shrine to ask for blessings from the deities, right?

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: As long as we put our heart into our offerings and make it so that the deities have a reason to reply, then any wish can be granted... right?

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you mentioning this all of a sudden... did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's like this...

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: Shouta... You went so eagerly to the shrine because of something like this...

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Yup! I wholeheartedly gave my offerings to the deity. However, those offerings kept on getting stolen... I thought the deity would blame me for this and won't watch over me anymore...

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: Silly child... Don't worry, that deity won't get mad at you for something small like this...

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Re—really? That's good...

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: But in the same way, that deity probably won't help someone just because of some offerings.

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: The reason people give offerings and ask for blessings isn't that they want their wish to be granted. Rather, those people gave their offerings to build a firm base for their confidence.

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: Confidence?

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: "As we've already told our wishes to the deity, we must try our best to make those wishes come true."

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: "With the deity watching over us, if we put in the effort, we'll succeed for sure."

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: With that kind of confidence, people are then willing to give it their all to fulfill their wishes. That's the reason why everyone gives offerings to the shrines.

dialogues.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
dialogues.text: At the end of the day... It's people that move the world. If we pray to deities and take no action, even if a deity wanted to help, it still won't know what it should do.

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: B—but when I gave offerings to the shrine before, that deity always directly helped me!

dialogues.speaker: Shouta
dialogues.text: That time with the fire, that mister who wanted to become stronger, and that comic book of mine...

response.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
response.text: Hmmm... You're right. It seems like that deity has a direct way of fulfilling wishes.

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: But, but... Not only did the exams not disappear, but that bully is still there. She still nags me every day about doing my school work...

response.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
response.text: Hmm, wait a minute. That person who's bullying you, what's her name? When did she appear?

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: She... She's... called... eh? What's her name again...

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: I think she entered school at the same time as me... No, no, I think a bit earlier... or was it later?

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: Weird... Why can't I remember anything? The only thing that I can remember is a girl telling me to study...

response.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
response.text: Hmmm, it seems like that deity has responded to your wishes again, and is currently helping you conquer your dislike for exams.

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: You mean that girl? The one who bullies me all the time? The deity sent her to force me to study!?

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: Noooo! I don't want to study, I don't want to take exams!

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: Waaaah! She's here again. She's right over there. She's coming over from the other side of the street!

response.speaker: Shouta
response.text: Can't you see her!? She's coming over with a huge pile of exam papers! Waaah! I don't wanna take an exaaaam!

response.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
response.text: It seems like that deity is very dedicated.

choices.text: That deity does things at its own pace...

response.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
response.text: However, under that deity's personal supervision, that child should be able to successfully pass his exams.

response.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
response.text: After all, I guess even deities can't stand that child's constant nagging...

response.speaker: Yayoi Nanatsuki
response.text: Huh? Wait. Why are there leaves on the road? They weren't here before...

choices.text: It doesn't feel like something a deity would do...
